In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the differential microstrip line loaded with MLCs is a good choice when the goal is to achieve a high level of isolation between two signals, while a single-ended microstrip line loaded by MLCs is the best choice to achieve a high return loss.

MLC resonators can be used as band-stop filters, as impedance matching circuits for single-ended and differential microstrip transmission lines, and as impedance matching circuits between differential microstrip lines and single-ended microstrip transmission lines.

MLC resonators loaded in differential microstrip lines are the most interesting and promising ones for the design of differential filters and matching networks, whereas MLC resonators coupled to single-ended microstrip transmission lines are the best candidates for the design of matching networks and bandpass filters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MLC resonators, in addition to the well-known ELC resonators, are a powerful tool for the design of differential and single-ended transmission lines.
, in the case of MLC resonators, the differential configuration is the preferred one, while, in the case for ELC resonators, it is the single-ended configuration.
the MLC resonator is the most promising candidate for the design of differential and single-ended microstrip line filters, especially in the case of narrowband and wideband filters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MLC resonators can be very effective in reducing the coupling between differential lines, and this can be used in the design of compact differential circuits.
MLC resonators can be used to realize compact, low-loss, high-isolation differential transmission lines.
